author: haiku
label: c2-nat-haiku-01
changes: Added a Terms section defining colour, instance, listener, target group, live and idle, /healthz, smoke tests, 5xx, migration and additive, retention, conditional write, T0 and Ts.
Defined the deploy lock as a conditional write that succeeds only if no other deploy holds it.
Explained the 5xx window: data runs up to now minus 2 minutes, the window never starts before Ts, and a zero-request window raises an alert.
Reworded step 3(c) so it says the idle colour must be empty, except for instances retention has already released.
Explained what to do when the result of the step 10 call is unknown: the listener read decides.
Defined the heartbeat in step 11 and said where it is written, since the watcher depends on it.
Step 13: stated the separate preconditions for a normal deploy and for a rollback, and said that the non-live colour is the one stopped.

Step 14: the queue starts after step 13 completes, not after R. The failed colour is not free until it is stopped, so after a rollback the queue waits about 30 minutes. The original wording was ambiguous here.
R2: said that step 1 reuses the existing image for the previous tag. This is a decision I made to remove ambiguity, not a change to the requirements.
Shortened and simplified sentences throughout, and kept the same step numbers, procedures, format and state table. No requirement, threshold or timing was changed.
Added a 'How to read this' overview that explains colours, the switch, the watch and the 30-minute retention in plain words before the detail.
Expanded the Terms section: defined colour, instance, target group, deploy lock, conditional write and queue, and removed jargon that was used without definition.
Explained the two sources of truth in plain words and stated that they are checked before each irreversible step.
Added a worked example for the 5xx window (at 12:10 the window is 12:03 to 12:08, never before Ts) and rephrased the 2-minute metric delay as 'data up to 2 minutes before now'.
Clarified step 3(c): the only allowed running instances are those released from retention and waiting for step 13.
Clarified step 4: the failed-index note now says not to fix it by redeploying.
Procedure A now states that step 10 falls under it only when the listener still forwards to the old target group, which matches step 10.
Step 10: the unknown-result case now says what the listener read means in both outcomes.
Step 11 now includes the zero-request alert rule from the decisions section, which was missing from the step.
Step 14 end-of-deploy wording now separates a normal deploy (status = complete) from a rollback (status stays rolled_back). The old text said 'complete' after a rollback, which contradicted step R.
Step 13 failure and precondition wording now says to shut nothing down and alert, instead of the less direct 'do not shut anything down'.
Kept the step numbers, procedure names, decisions, timings and the state table unchanged in substance.
Added a plain-language overview of the deploy flow, including why additive migrations keep the live release working.
Defined the deploy runner, heartbeat and idle target group in Terms. Clarified retention and the state item's role.
Made the two-truth check explicit: it runs before steps 10, R, R2 and 13, instead of 'each irreversible step'.
Step 2: separated the three cases (lock held or retention active, write failed for another reason, listener and state disagree).
Step 3(c): explained why the idle colour should already be empty, since step 14 only starts a queued deploy after step 13 stops the retained colour.
Step 5 and 6: made the wording of the T0 + 10 min limit consistent.
Step 10: spelled out the failure path after retries (read the listener, then continue to step 11 or go to procedure A).
5xx rule: added that a window never starts before Ts, with an example for an early evaluation.
Step 12: set retained to the old colour when promoting.
Procedure A: said where failed-instance logs go (CI run logs).
R: stated that traffic stays on the new colour until a repoint succeeds, and that the repoint is read back.
R2: said that the in-place branch writes the same state updates as R.
Left unchanged but not addressed: R2 run during the watch, when the deploy still holds the lock, is not specified. This needs a decision.
